summary: Tokyo's night runs in layers. 18:00 starts at an izakaya; 22:00 is a whisky bar or jazz kissa; 02:00 is Golden Gai or a Ni-chōme side-street club; the first train home is 04:45. Pace yourself.

scenes.title: Golden Gai
scenes.vibe: Tiny themed bars, survivor alleys, cash-only charm
scenes.body: Six alleys of 200+ hole-in-the-wall bars, each themed around music, film, a cult movie, a specific drink. Four to eight seats per bar. A ¥500-¥1,500 seat charge (otoshi) is standard and legit. Rotate bars — two drinks per stop is plenty.
scenes.tip: Look for an English menu outside the door — those bars actively welcome tourists. Skip bars with a black sign and no menu; they're members-only.

scenes.title: Shinjuku Ni-chōme
scenes.vibe: Queer nightlife capital of Asia; welcoming to everyone
scenes.body: Around 300 bars and clubs packed into a few short blocks, from tiny listening bars to the massive AiSOTOPE basement. One of the world's oldest gay districts.
scenes.tip: Starters: AiiRO Cafe (Sundays 14:00 streetside), Arty Farty (pop), Campy! Bar (camp cabaret), Eagle (bear). All tourist-friendly.

scenes.title: Jazz kissa listening bars
scenes.vibe: Silent listening rooms dedicated to vinyl worship
scenes.body: Post-war Tokyo's answer to scarce imports: tiny bars with master-grade hi-fi rigs where you sit, listen, and don't chat. Half a dozen originals remain — JBS Shibuya, Eagle Yotsuya, Meikyoku Kissa Lion in Shibuya, Dug Shinjuku.
scenes.tip: Phones silent, no photography, no conversation. Order a drink, listen to the side all the way through.

scenes.title: Craft beer trail
scenes.body: Japan's craft beer scene pushed past IPAs years ago — Shiga Kogen, Baird, Yo-Ho, Ise Kadoya. Tokyo's best concentration is between Shibuya and Ebisu on the Meguro River.
scenes.tip: Good trail: Beer Bar Ushitora (Shimokita) → Mikkeller Tokyo (Shibuya) → Goodbeer Faucets (Shibuya) → Devilcraft (Hamamatsucho) for Chicago-style deep-dish and a stacked tap list.

scenes.title: Whisky bars
scenes.vibe: Hushed counters, precision, Japanese whisky paradise
scenes.body: Ginza alone has over 40 whisky bars — cedar counters, pristine ice, bartenders in white coats. Japanese whisky allocations are tight; you'll find bottlings unavailable retail.
scenes.tip: Starters: Bar High Five (Ginza, no menu, tell them what you like), Star Bar (Ginza, cocktail-first), Zoetrope (Shinjuku, 300+ Japanese whiskies). Reserve or arrive early. ¥1,000-¥2,500 seat charge.

scenes.title: Izakaya crawl
scenes.neighborhood: Shinjuku Omoide Yokocho / Ebisu Yokocho / Ameyoko
scenes.body: The right introduction to Tokyo drinking. Yokocho means 'side alley' — a cluster of 8-seat shops selling skewers, sashimi, highballs, draft beer. Pay as you go, hop to the next.
scenes.tip: Ebisu Yokocho is the most tourist-accessible. Omoide Yokocho and Ameyoko are grittier, more authentic. Expect ¥500 otoshi charge per stop.

scenes.title: Clubs
scenes.body: Tokyo's club night runs very late — lineups peak at 02:00, first-trains at 04:45. Dress code is smart-casual; doormen turn away shorts and beach sandals.
scenes.tip: Contact Tokyo (Shibuya, underground dance), Womb (Shibuya, house/techno), ageHa (Shin-Kiba, mega-venue). Avoid touts in Roppongi — they steer into overpriced bars.

scenes.title: Rooftop bars with a view
scenes.vibe: Skyline dressing, quieter pace, pre-dinner or post-dinner
scenes.body: Tokyo's skyscraper hotels built their bars around the view. Dress smart, reserve ahead, drink slow.
scenes.tip: Picks: New York Bar at Park Hyatt (52F, the 'Lost in Translation' bar), Peak Lounge at Park Hyatt, Andaz Tavern (Toranomon), EDITION's Blue Room.
